identity: Hebrew Bible / Torah in the Arabic Van Dyck translation: Exodus 23:20-33 (the promise of the Angel and the conquest of Canaan) followed by Exodus 24:1-18 (the covenant ceremony, the elders' vision of God, and Moses' forty days on Sinai). Named by 449 tokens over 5 printed lines, median line 100 tokens - prose mode, PASS 2 applies.
law: SCRIPTURE: THE VERSE IS THE UNIT (my doctrine 0k, discovered on the Gospel of Luke in batch 7 and applied here for the first time to a second, independent scripture text). Nothing inside a verse cuts - not the consequential fa, not the coordinating wa, not an imperative, not bal, not a parallel clause pair. The verse boundary is the ONLY boundary. In batch 7 I lost 18 false cuts on Luke firing B1/F3 (fa), E6 (imperative), C5 (bal) and E1 (parallelism) inside verses; the reconstructed gold there was ~48 units over 685 tokens, i.e. ~14 tokens per unit, which is exactly the verse count of that passage. Here 449 tokens / 32 verses = 14.0 tokens per unit - the same signature, which is strong independent confirmation that the annotators segment scripture on the versification, not on syntax.
reasoning: I identified the passage and recovered the versification rather than parsing syntax, because 0k says the versification IS the answer. (7) @412 'wa-fi al-yawm al-sabi' - a fronted time frame mid-verse; v16 contains it, so NO cut, which is the one place where 0n must yield to 0k.
